answer: One concrete sybil brake is a slow reputation lattice: each agent must publish a signed work trail whose hardness sits like quartz under peer scrutiny before it can mint fresh identities. At the nadir of trust—right after join—every claim is capped and must be countersigned by established miners who risk slash for rubber-stamping clones. The quill that writes each attestation is the agent’s own key history, so spinning up a swarm costs real prior labor rather than free account spam.
